population.e: The population of New Jersey will not stand for this!

portrait.d: A painting or other picture of a person, especially the head and shoulders.
portrait.e: The author painted a good portrait of urban life in New York in his latest book.

possible.e: Jones is a possible for the new opening in sales.

possibly.d: Perhaps; indicates that the proposition may be true (is not certainly false) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker.
possibly.e: Possibly, they will make gains in the midterm elections.

post office.d: A place (building, office, shop, or counter) concerned with the business of delivering letters, post or mail and selling stamps, etc.

pour.d: To cause (liquid, or liquid-like substance) to flow in a stream, either out of a container or into it.

power.d: The ability to do or undergo something.
power.e: He has lost the power to speak.

powerful.d: Having, or capable of exerting power, potency or influence.
powerful.e: Not very many (of them) had been damaged.

prediction.d: A statement of what will happen in the future.

prefer.d: To be in the habit of choosing something rather than something else; to favor; to like better.

prepare.e: We prepared the spacecraft for takeoff.

pressure.d: A force applied to a surface, calculated by amount of force that is applied over a given area divided by the size of this area; force per unit area.
pressure.e: She applied too much pressure to the door handle, and it snapped.

pretend.d: To speak or behave so as to give a false or simulated appearance.
pretend.e: You don't have to pretend that the soup tastes fine.

prevent.d: To stop (an outcome); to keep from (doing something).
prevent.e: I brush my teeth regularly to prevent tooth decay.

pride.d: The quality or state of being proud. A sense of one's own worth; reasonable self-esteem and satisfaction (in oneself, in one's work, one's family, etc).
pride.e: He swelled with pride as he held the trophy. His family watched with pride from the bleachers.

principal.d: The money originally invested or loaned, on which basis interest and returns are calculated.
principal.e: A portion of your mortgage payment goes to reduce the principal, and the rest covers interest.

print.d: Of, relating to, or writing for printed publications.
print.e: a print edition of a book

private.d: A soldier of the lowest rank in the army.
private.e: Her address is private; you can't have it.

pro.d: An advantage of something, especially when contrasted with its disadvantages (cons).
pro.e: He is pro exercise but against physical exertion, quite a conundrum.

probably.e: She probably has arrived by now.

produce.d: To yield, make or manufacture; to generate.

professional.d: A person who belongs to a profession

progressive.d: A person who actively favors or strives for progress towards improved conditions, as in society or government.

pronunciation.d: The formal or informal way in which a word is made to sound when spoken.

proper.d: Something set apart for a special use.

provide.d: To make a living; earn money for necessities.
provide.e: It is difficult to provide for my family working on minimum wage.

public.d: The people in general, regardless of membership of any particular group.
public.e: Members of the public may not proceed beyond this point.

publish.d: To issue (something, such as printed work) for distribution and/or sale.
publish.e: Most of the sketches Faulkner published in 1925 appeared in the Sunday magazine section of the New Orleans Times-Picayune.

pull.e: He gave the hair a sharp pull and it came out.

purpose.d: An objective to be reached; a target; an aim; a goal.

pursue.d: To follow urgently, originally with intent to capture or harm; to chase.
pursue.e: Her rival pursued a quite different course.

quality.e: Quality of life is usually determined by health, education, and income.

quite.d: (heading) To the greatest extent or degree; completely, entirely.

raincoat.d: A waterproof coat to be worn in the rain.

raise.d: To cause to rise; to lift or elevate.
raise.e: to raise your hand if you want to say something; to raise your walking stick to defend yourself

range.d: A line or series of mountains, buildings, etc.

rate.e: At the height of his powers, he was producing pictures at the rate of four a year.

rather.d: Used to specify a choice or preference; preferably, in preference to. (Now usually followed by than)
rather.e: I'd rather not have spent all the money, but it really was an emergency.

rating.d: present participle and gerund of rate
rating.e: They have a poor credit rating.

raw.d: (sugar refining, sugar trade) An unprocessed sugar; a batch of such.

ray.d: A beam of light or radiation.
ray.e: I saw a ray of light through the clouds.

realize.d: To make real; to convert from the imaginary or fictitious into reality; to bring into real existence
realize.e: The objectives of the project were never fully realized.

receipt.d: The act of receiving, or the fact of having been received.
receipt.e: A balance payable on receipt of the goods.

receive.d: An operation in which data is received.
receive.e: She received many presents for her birthday.

recent.d: Having happened a short while ago.

receptionist.d: An employee (such as a secretary) who works in reception (receiving visitors and/or calls) for a person or business, especially an office.

record.d: An item of information put into a temporary or permanent physical medium.
record.e: The person had a record of the interview so she could review her notes.

recycle.e: Both paper and plastic can be recycled.

reflect.d: To bend back (light, etc.) from a surface.
reflect.e: A mirror reflects the light that shines on it.

refrigerator.d: A household appliance used for keeping food fresh by refrigeration (short form fridge).

regret.d: To feel sorry about (a thing that has or has not happened), afterthink: to wish that a thing had not happened, that something else had happened instead.
regret.e: I regret that I have to do this, but I don't have a choice.

regular.d: Bound by religious rule; belonging to a monastic or religious order (often as opposed to secular).
regular.e: regular clergy, in distinction from the secular clergy

regularly.e: We regularly buy lottery tickets from the corner store.

relax.e: to relax a rope or cord

relaxed.d: Made slack or feeble; weak, soft.
relaxed.e: The relaxed rules were greatly tightened after the lawsuit.

release.d: The event of setting (someone or something) free (e.g. hostages, slaves, prisoners, caged animals, hooked or stuck mechanisms).
release.e: He released his grasp on the lever.

remain.d: (chiefly in the plural) That which is left; relic; remainder.
remain.e: There was no food in the house, so I had to remain hungry.

remind.d: To cause one to experience a memory (of someone or something); to bring to the notice or consideration (of a person).

remote.d: An element of broadcast programming originating away from the station's or show's control room.
remote.e: A remote operator may control the vehicle with a wireless handset.

rent.d: A payment made by a tenant at intervals in order to occupy a property.
rent.e: I rented a house from my friend's parents for a year.

repair.d: To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
repair.e: to repair a house, a road, a shoe, a ship

replace.d: To restore to a former place, position, condition, etc.; to put back
replace.e: When you've finished using the telephone, please replace the handset.

reply.d: A written or spoken response; part of a conversation.
reply.e: Joanne replied to Pete's insult with a slap to his face.

report.d: A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).
report.e: A report by the telecommunications ministry on the phone network revealed a severe capacity problem.

represent.d: To present again or anew; to present by means of something standing in the place of; to exhibit the counterpart or image of; to typify.
represent.e: The sculptor represented a horse in bronze.

request.d: Act of requesting (with the adposition at in the presence of possessives, and on in their absence).
request.e: I have requested that the furniture be moved back to its original position.

research.d: Diligent inquiry or examination to seek or revise facts, principles, theories, applications, etc. (that are currently available, or that are familiar to oneself).
research.e: The research station that houses Wang and his team is outside Lijiang, a city of about 1.2 million people.

response.d: An answer or reply, or something in the nature of an answer or reply.

retire.d: To stop working on a permanent basis, usually because of old age or illness.
retire.e: I have decided to retire from football at the end of the season after the World Cup.

retired.d: Secluded from society (of a lifestyle, activity etc.); private, quiet.

return.e: I expect the house to be spotless upon my return.

reunion.d: The process or act of reuniting.
reunion.e: The reunion took forever, but it was worth it.

reveal.d: The outer side of a window or door frame; the jamb.
reveal.e: The comedian had been telling us about his sleep being disturbed by noise. Then came the reveal: he was sleeping on a bed in a department store.

rhythm.d: The variation of strong and weak elements (such as duration, accent) of sounds, notably in speech or music, over time; a beat or meter.
rhythm.e: Dance to the rhythm of the music.

road.d: A way used for travelling between places, originally one wide enough to allow foot passengers and horses to travel, now (US) usually one surfaced with asphalt or concrete and designed to accommodate many vehicles travelling in both directions. In the UK both senses are heard: a country road is the same as a country lane.
road.e: We travelled to the seaside by road.

roast.d: A cut of meat suited to roasting
roast.e: to roast meat on a spit

rob.d: To steal from, especially using force or violence.
rob.e: The best way to rob a bank is to own one.

robbery.d: The act or practice of robbing.

rock.e: Pearl Rock near Cape Cod is so named because the morning sun makes it gleam like a pearl.

root.d: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
root.e: The cuttings are starting to root.

rope.d: Thick strings, yarn, monofilaments, metal wires, or strands of other cordage that are twisted together to form a stronger line.
rope.e: Nylon rope is usually stronger than similar rope made of plant fibers.

roughly.d: In a rough manner; without kindness, softness, or gentleness.

round.d: Of shape: Circular or cylindrical; having a circular cross-section in one direction.
round.e: We sat at a round table to make conversation easier.

royal.d: Of or relating to a monarch or his (or her) family.

ruin.d: (sometimes in the plural) The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
ruin.e: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

rush.d: Any of several stiff plants of the genus Juncus, or the family Juncaceae, having hollow or pithy stems and small flowers, and often growing in marshes or near water.
